skill.name: nestjs-git-commit-pr-message
skill.description: Prepares and publishes intentional Git changes for NestJS projects. Use when the user asks to commit, push, create or update a pull request, prepare changelog or release text, or verify a GitHub Pages deployment after publication. It inspects the complete diff, preserves unrelated work, scans staged content for secrets, matches repository commit conventions, runs relevant checks, and performs only the explicitly requested remote actions. When other skills also apply, reconcile ownership before mutation.
skill.summary: Prepare verified NestJS commits, pull requests, and release text while preserving unrelated work and respecting publication permissions.
skill.author: amirtaherkhani

content.user_title: Prepare NestJS Commits and Pull Requests
content.value_statement: Mixed changes and unclear publication requests can produce misleading commits or unintended remote updates. This skill guides verified Git changes and accurate messages within authorized scope.
actual_capabilities: Inspect staged and unstaged changes, branch history, and remotes to establish intended commit scope.
Review staged content for plausible secrets and prohibited artifacts before committing.
Draft commit messages that match repository conventions and verified changes.
Run relevant project checks and report executed, unavailable, or failing checks accurately.
Commit, push, and create or update pull requests when authorized by the requested workflow.
Prepare changelog or release text and follow CI or GitHub Pages results for the pushed revision.
limitations: Requires Git and repository access; GitHub operations also require an authenticated connector or gh CLI.
Secret review relies on contextual inspection and does not guarantee detection of every credential.
Uses existing project checks and cannot report successful verification when required tools or scripts are unavailable.
Does not authorize merges, release publication, deployment, or history rewriting through a routine push or pull request request.

use_cases.title: Commit an isolated NestJS fix
use_cases.description: Prepare a verified commit for one feature while preserving unrelated staged and unstaged work.

use_cases.title: Prepare a reviewable pull request
use_cases.description: Publish an authorized branch update with an accurate summary, compatibility decisions, and actual verification results.

use_cases.title: Report release and documentation status
use_cases.description: Draft release notes and verify whether the pushed revision triggers CI or GitHub Pages without assuming deployment success.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a commit message
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the staged NestJS changes and draft a commit message matching repository history. Do not commit, push, or modify files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: describe an existing staged change.

prompt_templates.title: Commit only the intended fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Commit the NestJS auth fix after relevant checks and staged secret review. Preserve unrelated dashboard changes. Do not push.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: isolate a commit in a mixed worktree.

prompt_templates.title: Open a draft pull request
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify the payments feature, commit its intended scope, push to the confirmed remote, and open or update a draft pull request.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: complete an authorized publication workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Verify publication and prepare release text
prompt_templates.prompt: Push the verified documentation commit, follow CI for its exact SHA, and report whether Pages updated. Draft release notes without tagging, merging, or publishing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine revision-specific follow-up with release preparation.

best_practices: Specify the intended files and whether the task permits committing, pushing, creating a pull request, or preparing release text.
Review staged changes and relevant check results before authorizing publication.
Verify the target remote, branch, and exact revision before accepting CI or deployment claims.
anti_patterns: Stage every changed file when the worktree includes unrelated edits.
Include live credentials or personal data in commits, pull request bodies, or verification reports.
Treat a branch push as permission to merge, release, force-push, or claim a completed deployment.

faq.question: Does drafting a message create a commit?
faq.answer: No. A message-only request permits inspection and drafting, not committing or pushing.

faq.question: Does committing also push the branch?
faq.answer: No. A commit request permits staging the confirmed scope and committing. Pushing requires authorization.

faq.question: Are Conventional Commits always required?
faq.answer: No. The skill matches repository history and rules, using Conventional Commits only when compatible.

faq.question: What happens when a plausible secret is staged?
faq.answer: The workflow stops before committing and reports the location and category without reproducing the secret value.

faq.question: What does GitHub integration require?
faq.answer: GitHub operations require an authenticated connector or gh CLI. The skill verifies repository and branch targets before writes.

faq.question: Does a documentation push always update GitHub Pages?
faq.answer: No. The workflow must match the pushed ref and paths. Deployment success requires observed completion for the exact revision.
